cases.sentence: Взволнованное ___ Европы улеглось в свои бepeгà.
cases.explain: «историческое море» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Seven years had passed. The storm-tossed sea of European history had subsided within its shores and seemed to have become calm. But the mysterious forces that move humanity (mysterious because the laws of their motion are unknown to us) continued to operate.

cases.sentence: Оно казалось затихшим; но ___, двигающие человечество (таинственные потому, что законы, определяющие их движение, неизвестны нам) продолжали свое действие.
cases.explain: «таинственные силы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Seven years had passed. The storm-tossed sea of European history had subsided within its shores and seemed to have become calm. But the mysterious forces that move humanity (mysterious because the laws of their motion are unknown to us) continued to operate.

cases.sentence: Несмотря на то, что поверхность ___ казалась неподвижною, так же непрерывно, как движение времени, двигалось человечество.
cases.explain: «исторического моря» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Though the surface of the sea of history seemed motionless, the movement of humanity went on as unceasingly as the flow of time. Various groups of people formed and dissolved, the coming formation and dissolution of kingdoms and displacement of peoples was in course of preparation.

cases.sentence: Слагались, разлагались ___ людских сцеплений; подготовлялись причины образования и разложения государств, перемещений народов.
cases.explain: «различные группы» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Though the surface of the sea of history seemed motionless, the movement of humanity went on as unceasingly as the flow of time. Various groups of people formed and dissolved, the coming formation and dissolution of kingdoms and displacement of peoples was in course of preparation.

cases.sentence: ___, не направлялось как прежде, порывами от одного берега к другому: оно бурлило в глубине.
cases.explain: «Историческое море» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The sea of history was not driven spasmodically from shore to shore as previously. It was seething in its depths. Historic figures were not borne by the waves from one shore to another as before. They now seemed to rotate on one spot. The historical figures at the head of armies, who formerly reflected the movement of the masses by ordering wars, campaigns, and battles, now reflected the restless movement by political and diplomatic combinations, laws, and treaties.

cases.explain: «исторических лиц» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The historians call this activity of the historical figures “the reaction.”

cases.sentence: Описывая деятельность этих ___, бывших, по их мнению, причиною того, что́ они называют реакцией, историки строго осуждают их.
cases.explain: «исторических лиц» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: In dealing with this period they sternly condemn the historical personages who, in their opinion, caused what they describe as the reaction. All the well-known people of that period, from Alexander and Napoleon to Madame de Staël, Photius, Schelling, Fichte, Chateaubriand, and the rest, pass before their stern judgment seat and are acquitted or condemned according to whether they conduced to progress or to reaction.

cases.sentence: В настоящей ___ от гимназиста до ученого историка, нет человека, который бы не бросил своего камушка в Александра за неправильные поступки его в этот период царствования.
cases.explain: «русской литературе» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: There is no one in Russian literature now, from schoolboy essayist to learned historian, who does not throw his little stone at Alexander for things he did wrong at this period of his reign.

cases.sentence: Мало того, одновременно мы находим в истории совершенно ___ на то, что́ было зло и что́ было благо: одни данную Польше конституцию и Священный Союз ставят в заслугу, другие в укор Александру.
cases.explain: «противоположные взгляды» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: But even if we assume that fifty years ago Alexander I was mistaken in his view of what was good for the people, we must inevitably assume that the historian who judges Alexander will also after the lapse of some time turn out to be mistaken in his view of what is good for humanity. This assumption is all the more natural and inevitable because, watching the movement of history, we see that every year and with each new writer, opinion as to what is good for mankind changes; so that what once seemed good, ten years later seems bad, and vice versa. And what is more, we find at one and the same time quite contradictory views as to what is bad and what is good in history: some people regard giving a constitution to Poland and forming the Holy Alliance as praiseworthy in Alexander, while others regard it as blameworthy.
